question: None shared. Despite its title, P-208 (Lim et al., Front Aging Neurosci 2022) runs only a cross-sectional three-way diagnostic classification (CN vs MCI vs AD) of ADNI1 baseline sMRI axial slices; it has no conversion labels and no pMCI/sMCI experiment. P-78 (Xu et al., ESWA 2026) predicts 36-month MCI-to-AD conversion (pMCI vs sMCI) from longitudinal sMRI. Current three-class diagnosis and binary conversion prognosis are different clinical questions. The channel (structural MRI) and the cohort family (ADNI) are shared.
metric: Nominally accuracy in both, but not the same quantity. P-208's is a three-class, image-level test accuracy (chance about 33%); P-78's is a binary, subject-level conversion accuracy (chance about 50%).

figures.P-208: Three-class CN/MCI/AD test accuracy 78.57% (VGG-16; CNN from scratch 72.70%, ResNet-50 75.71%) on a random hold-out of 2D slice images from 819 subjects (229 CN/398 MCI/192 AD). No interval printed. For reference only, Wilson at the subject level with n about 164 (20% of 819): z^2/n = 0.02342, centre 0.7792, half-width 0.0624, CI [0.717, 0.842]. The image-level test n is larger, which would narrow this.
figures.P-78: pMCI vs sMCI, 36-month window. Four-timepoint (QTP) ablation on internal Dataset B (101 subjects): accuracy 90.7%, AUC 0.871; Wilson with n = 101: centre 0.8921, half-width 0.0576, CI [0.835, 0.950]. Single-visit external test (Dataset A, ADNI-3 + OASIS-3, 173 subjects): accuracy 0.827 (printed 95% CI 0.769-0.884), AUC 0.858 (0.803-0.918).

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-208 reports no conversion result, and P-78 reports no three-class diagnostic accuracy. Neither paper places a figure on the other's contrast.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: 78.57% and 90.7% are below 0.97. Note that P-208 splits at the image level with up to three slices per subject, which may put slices of one subject in both train and test; this is not the Section 3.5 exclusion.
reason: P-208 is a three-way CN/MCI/AD diagnostic study with no conversion endpoint, while P-78 predicts 36-month pMCI vs sMCI conversion. There is no shared clinical question (condition 1), and the accuracies have different class structures and chance levels. The ledger's 'T2' label for P-208 follows its title, not its experiment (condition 6).

quotes.quote: we proposed a multiclass classification method based on 3D T1-weight brain sMRI images from the ADNI database. Axial brain images were extracted from 3D MRI and fed into the convolutional neural network (CNN) for multiclass classification.
Implementing CNN to perform multiclass classification (3-way) to classify cognitively normal (CN), MCI, and AD subjects.
A total of 819 subjects (229 CN, 398 with MCI, and 192 with AD) were enrolled at baseline.
the reported classification performance on test data is accuracy of 72.70, 78.57, and 75.71%, respectively
subjects diagnosed with MCI at any follow-up visit and who progressed to AD within three years are defined as pMCI.
The model achieved peak performance with QTP, recording an AUC of 87.1 % and an ACC of 90.7 %.
attaining the highest scores in AUC (0.858), ACC (0.827), F1-score (0.824), SPE (0.890), and PRE (0.886).
